newsitem.title: UK: BoE's George says no real change in RPIX target.
newsitem.headline: BoE's George says no real change in RPIX target.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Wednesday that the new-style inflation target did not in any real sense represent a loosening of policy.

"I don't think there is any substantial or significant change in the degree of intended tightening," he told the House of Commons Treasury Select Committee. "Technically you can argue it's a marginal loosening but that certainly hasn't featured in market perceptions."

Under Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's new regime, the Bank is required to hit a target of 2.5 percent for underlying inflation. If RPIX strays more than one percentage point either side of that target, the Bank may be required to write an open letter explaining why.
George said the one percentage point on either side was not in any sense a target range but a trigger point for the open letter to the Chancellor.
He said there might be good reasons for remaining more than 1.0 percentage point away from the target for some time, if the economy was rattled by an external shock.
The previous Chancellor, Kenneth Clarke, had a target for RPIX of 2.5 percent or less.
